title: AI Act
edition: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 • original OJ edition, 12 July 2024 • EN

passages.text: The system definition combines machine-based operation, varying autonomy, possible adaptiveness and inference from inputs to outputs that can influence environments.

Provider covers developing or commissioning a system and placing it on the market or putting it into service under an own name or trademark. Deployer concerns use under own authority, excluding personal non-professional activity.
Intended purpose includes the provider-specified use, context and conditions. Instructions inform deployers about purpose and proper use. Substantial modification is separately defined.
The listed recruitment and selection uses include targeted job advertising, analysis and filtering of applications, and evaluation of candidates. The list must be read with Article 6.

Annex III systems are classified as high-risk, subject to the paragraph 3 qualification concerning significant risk and the specified procedural, improvement, pattern-detection or preparatory tasks. Annex III profiling systems remain high-risk. A provider concluding that a system is not high-risk must document its assessment before market placement or service and comply with the stated registration obligation.

Risk management is a documented, maintained, continuous lifecycle process. It identifies and evaluates foreseeable risks and misuse, considers monitoring information, and adopts appropriate measures. Risk is not just a single score.

Training, validation and testing datasets have distinct roles. Governance covers origin, preparation, assumptions, suitability, bias and data gaps. Quality is assessed in view of intended purpose; paragraph 6 limits these requirements to testing datasets for systems not using model-training techniques.
Technical documentation is prepared before market placement or service, kept current, and supports assessment against the high-risk requirements. Annex IV specifies its minimum content.

High-risk systems provide automatic event recording to support traceability, monitoring and identification of risks or substantial modifications. The additional biometric-specific fields in paragraph 3 are not general recruitment requirements.

Instructions identify the provider and explain purpose, capabilities, limitations, tested performance, foreseeable risks and oversight. They also describe relevant maintenance and logging arrangements. Several information items are qualified by applicability, appropriateness or relevance.

Oversight measures may be built into a system or identified for implementation by the deployer. As appropriate and proportionate, assigned people can understand limitations, monitor, interpret outputs, avoid automation bias, override outputs and interrupt operation.

Specified changes to branding, substantial modification or intended purpose can transfer provider responsibilities for a particular system. The conditions and qualifications must remain attached to that role change.

Deployers use high-risk systems according to instructions and assign oversight to natural persons with competence, training, authority and support. Relevant, representative input data is required insofar as the deployer controls that data.

Deployers retain automatically generated logs insofar as those logs are under their control. The period must suit the intended purpose and be at least six months, unless applicable Union or national law provides otherwise. Financial institutions have an additional documentation qualification.
Risk combines the probability of harm occurring and the severity of that harm.
